messages.author: f233727408cbb3b6
messages.subject: Label plot()
parts:
Hi all !

We are studying the mandible shape's correlation to dietary variables and body mass in mammals. I have completed my analysis and am struggling with some visualization aspects. I have plotted many of my proc.D.pgls models in a format similar to this :
 
plot(glm_List1[[2]], type="regression",reg.type = "RegScore",
     predictor = Mandshape_env$CentroidSize,pch=19,cex=3,
     col=alpha(Majrules_pointcols,0.6),
     main="Shape~log10Csize")

I'd like to display the specimen names on this plot to get a better idea of the distribution and further inspect the outliers, and I've tried to get the specimen names to display on the plot but nothing seems to be working.

Is there any way to implement this?  Alternatively, is there any way to extract the values on the y axis of this plot? 

If this has already been addressed in an earlier thread, simply directing me to this would suffice and I apologize for not being able to find it myself. 

Kind regards, 
Wade Harris

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Label plot()
parts:
Dear Wade,

The plot function you are using is an S3 generic function, so any of the plot-associated functions, like points, main, text, arrows, etc., can all be used.  The following is an example of how to do what you seek.  Note that you need to name a plot object for this to work (I used P).  It is not really logical, because the centroid size is not available from coordinates lacking scale, but it should help elucidate how you can accomplish your goal.  Check out the text() help file for more guidance.

Best,
Mike

> library(geomorph)
> data("plethspecies")
> Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethspecies$land)

Performing GPA
  |=====================================================| 100%

Making projections... Finished!
> fit <- procD.lm(coords ~ log(Csize), data = Y.gpa,
+                 phy = plethspecies$phy)
> P <- plot(fit, type = "regression",
+           reg.type = "RegScore",
+           predictor = Y.gpa$Csize,
+           pch=19,cex=3,
+           col = gray(0.5, 0.2),
+           xlab = "Centroid Size")
> 
> P$plot_args$y
                          [,1]
P_cinereus        0.0048198878
P_electromorphus -0.0071050592
P_hoffmani       -0.0022133547
P_hubrichti      -0.0001967686
P_nettingi        0.0060472799
P_richmondi      -0.0034263769
P_serratus       -0.0009952005
P_shenandoah      0.0053734907
P_virginia       -0.0023038985
> P$plot_args$x
      P_cinereus P_electromorphus       P_hoffmani 
        1.000195         1.000134         1.000130 
     P_hubrichti       P_nettingi      P_richmondi 
        1.000226         1.000642         1.000129 
      P_serratus     P_shenandoah       P_virginia 
        1.000379         1.000292         1.000335 
> 
> text(P$plot_args$x, P$plot_args$y, 
+      names(P$plot_args$x), pos = 4)
